#5586. The VA Home Loan Benefits Giving Military Buyers an Edge in a Tough Market

Thanks to the bravery and sacrifices of our veterans and active military, our country’s civilians can live the American dream in safety. So how fitting is it that one tangible way our country says "thank you for your service" to current and former members of the military is through the Department of Veterans Affairs home loan benefit?

These unique mortgage options allow veterans and those still serving to acquire their own piece of the American dream by potentially qualifying for homes they might have otherwise thought were out of reach.

In July 2025, HR 1815, the VA Home Loan Reform Act, passed with bipartisan support through the House, Senate, and President Donald Trump.

Backed by the National Association of Realtors®, the bill made permanent a policy allowing veterans to directly pay their real estate agents—ensuring equal access to the housing market. It also establishes a partial claims program to help veterans catch up on missed mortgage payments.

"The VA Home Loan Guaranty is a unique government program that allows veterans to purchase a home without a down payment," said Shannon McGahn, NAR executive vice president and chief advocacy officer at the time.

"We are grateful to the House of Representatives and the Senate for passing this measure and providing veterans and active-duty service members the same advantages as other buyers in a competitive real estate market. NAR remains committed to protecting the brave men and women who serve this country in the armed forces and ensuring they are given equal opportunities to achieve the American dream of homeownership."

Veterans, active-duty service personnel, and select reservists or National Guard members are among those who can qualify for VA loans (find eligibility requirements here). Wondering what some of the benefits of a VA loan might be? Here are five of the most popular features.

This is one of the most valuable and touted benefits—and for good reason. Saving enough for a down payment can be the biggest obstacle to buying a home. But a VA loan eliminates that roadblock.

“Most of the buyers I work with don’t have extra resources available, so the fact that they can purchase a home with zero down makes the transaction feasible,” says Benny Dinsmore, himself a veteran and a real estate agent with Coldwell Banker in Frisco, TX.

Qualified VA buyers don’t have a down payment requirement in most cases.

But beware: The “no money down” aspect of a VA loan shouldn’t be confused with “no money out of pocket,” a common misconception, notes Michael Garcia, broker and owner of Weichert, Realtors–TQS in Lake Worth, FL.

A VA purchase transaction still requires closing costs and often includes an earnest money deposit (a negotiated amount of money that the buyer puts in escrow to essentially "hold" the house).

“However, that money will often come back at the closing, when the title company will write a check back to the veteran on the spot for the total amount that was put into escrow,” Garcia says.

The required credit score for a VA loan can be lower than for a conventional loan—around 620 for a VA loan compared with a range of 650 to 700 for most conventional loans.

In addition, the required debt-to-income ratio for VA loans is often more flexible than for conventional mortgages.

“It allows someone with less-than-perfect credit and some debt to still be able to qualify for a loan,” Dinsmore says.

Most conventional buyers have to pay private mortgage insurance if they put less than 20% down. Federal Housing Administration loans come with their own forms of mortgage insurance. But a VA loan waives that insurance requirement.

"This can be a big savings in monthly payments," says real estate agent Twila Lukavich, with Russell Real Estate Services in Cleveland.

Even though there's no mortgage insurance, there is a "funding fee"—an upfront cost applied to every purchase loan or refinance. The proceeds help the VA cover losses on the few loans that go into default. But borrowers can roll it into their monthly payment, or pay it all at once. Plus, it's tax-deductible. And veterans with a service-connected disability and select others don’t have to pay the funding fee at all.

Legally, veterans might have to pay for certain closing costs, which include the following:

But there are some fees that veterans don't have to pay. And the VA allows lenders to charge no more than 1% to cover the costs of originating and underwriting the loan.

Furthermore, even those costs can be rolled into the loan. So, for example, if the purchase price is $280,000, the veteran might offer $300,000 and ask for 3% back to cover the closing costs.

“In this way, the veteran is essentially financing their closing costs into the loan, meaning less out of pocket at the start,” Dinsmore explains.

When a home that a veteran is considering purchasing is having trouble reaching the purchase price during the appraisal process, buyers and lenders can ask the VA appraiser to consider adjusting the valuation before making a final determination.

Appraisers notify lenders in the event the appraised value is likely to come in low, giving buyers and real estate agents 48 hours to supply additional information that the appraiser might not be aware of to help justify the home’s value.

"Typically, I assemble an itemized list of upgrades and improvements that the seller has performed on the home in the past three years that the appraiser didn’t know about, and therefore didn’t include in the home value," Lukavich says.

This process "gives the agents an opportunity to assist the appraiser in making sure they have the whole picture of the home and gives the local agent an opening to help an appraiser be educated on specific local values,” she adds.

It's just another benefit of VA loans aimed at helping our servicemen/women buy the home of their dreams.

Cathie Ericson writes about real estate, finance, and health. She lives in Portland, OR.

#5585. Blumenthal Investigation Targets Binance, Tether and Trump Crypto Firms as Senate Sets January Deadline

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal, following his investigation, has given Binance, Tether, and two Trump crypto companies until January 4, 2027, to produce records. The investigation is examining alleged illicit cryptocurrency flows and potential conflicts of interest involving the Trump administration.

The incoming chair of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations sent letters to the four companies on November 5, and we learn today that Blumenthal warned that failing to provide the requested information could force the panel to consider alternative enforcement measures.

World Liberty Financial and Fight Fight Fight LLC, the company behind the TRUMP memecoin, face separate questions about foreign investments and potential conflicts of interest. Binance and Tether face scrutiny over alleged illicit financial activity, including Iran-linked cryptocurrency transactions.

The latest letters renew congressional pressure following months of investigations and previous requests for information. November 30 marks the initial document production deadline, while January 4, 2027, is the final deadline for voluntary compliance. Blumenthal, in his investigation, warned that the Senate could pursue alternative measures if the companies fail to cooperate.

🇺🇸 BREAKING: U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal sends letter to Tether, Binance, and two Trump-linked crypto firms demanding records in the ongoing Senate investigations before January 4, 2027.The incoming chair of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations is examining… pic.twitter.com/MwFVngVngm

For now, the letters do not announce subpoenas or formal enforcement actions. Instead, they establish a final window for the companies to provide records before the subcommittee considers further steps.

Blumenthal currently serves as the ranking member of the investigative panel. He is expected to become its chair when Democrats assume control of the Senate subcommittee. This transition could strengthen his ability to pursue compulsory document requests.

The Binance inquiry has already faced several rounds of correspondence. Blumenthal first requested information about the exchange’s compliance practices and potential Iran-linked transactions in February 2026.

He renewed those demands in April, questioning whether Binance had provided misleading information about its handling of suspicious transactions. The exchange has disputed allegations surrounding its compliance practices.

The Tether investigation gained momentum following a September 28 report from Democratic investigators on the Senate subcommittee. The report examined 846 cryptocurrency wallets sanctioned or targeted for seizure because of their alleged connections to Iran and regional proxy groups.

Investigators found that 84% of those wallets had transacted exclusively or almost exclusively in USDT. They described Tether’s stablecoin as a significant financial channel within Iran’s shadow banking network.

Tether has pushed back against the findings, arguing that its compliance teams proactively freeze suspicious wallets. CEO Paolo Ardoino also claimed the company froze Iran-linked addresses an average of four weeks before official sanctions designations.

Meanwhile, the Trump investigation focuses on his two crypto ventures, World Liberty Financial and Fight Fight Fight LLC. Blumenthal originally opened the inquiry in May 2025 following concerns about potential conflicts of interest involving Trump.

Investigators are examining foreign investments, financial relationships with overseas entities, and potential violations of government ethics requirements. Fight Fight Fight LLC operates the Official Trump memecoin, while World Liberty Financial is associated with the Trump family’s crypto business.

The senator also hosted a public forum in July 2026 examining the Trump family’s crypto companies. That proceeding included testimony from TRUMP investors who reported losing thousands of dollars.

The latest requests connect two major political and financial investigations. One examines potential sanctions-related crypto activity, while the other focuses on foreign money and presidential business interests.

The January deadline could become a significant test of congressional oversight. Blumenthal will soon lead the investigative panel as it pursues records from companies connected to some of the biggest names in crypto.

#5584. Meta introduces Muse Ember to power cost-efficient AI agents

Meta Platforms Inc. today introduced Muse Ember, an entry-level artificial intelligence model that costs significantly less than the competition.

Notably, it’s the first AI that the company trained using Muse Wonder. The latter algorithm is the Facebook parent’s flagship large language model. Meta didn’t specify which part of the workflow it automated with Muse Wonder.

One possibility is that the company used it to perform post-training, the task of honing a model’s capabilities by training it on additional data. Thinking Machines Labs Inc. recently demonstrated that even a relatively small LLM can run post-training runs end-to-end. Anthropic PBC, for its part, last week revealed that its AI models could soon gain the ability to significantly accelerate machine learning research.

Applications often use frontier LLMs such as Muse Wonder as part of AI ensembles. When a user enters a request, the frontier LLM splits it into smaller tasks and assigns them to agents powered by a lower-cost model. Meta says Muse Ember is specifically optimized to play the latter role.

The company evaluated the model using the Artificial Analysis Index, which aggregates nine AI benchmarks spanning use cases such as coding and financial analysis. Meta says that Muse Ember matched the score of Anthropic’s entry-level Claude Haiku 5.5 model at about a third the price. It also outperformed OpenAI Group PBC’s comparable GPT-6 Luna algorithm.

The same internal evaluation saw Meta test Muse Ember and the two rival models across nine other benchmarks. All three algorithms were in “max” mode, which means they used the maximum amount of hardware at their disposal instead of prioritizing cost-efficiency. Muse Ember outperformed Haiku and Luna across seven of the benchmarks.

The area where the model appears to have the biggest edge is business task automation. Whereas most of Muse Ember’s benchmark results were only a few percentage points better than those of Haiku and Luna, it clocked a 17% lead on AutomationBench-AA. It’s a collection of 657 tasks that span popular cloud applications such as Gmail and Salesforce.

Muse Ember has a context window of 1 million tokens, which enables it to ingest lengthy business documents. Users can also include images, audio and video in their prompts. The model generates responses up to 512,000 tokens in length.

Muse Ember is available through Meta’s Model API for 10 cents per million input tokens and 50 cents per million output tokens. A built-in cache can reuse frequently used prompts to avoid duplicate processing. When the feature is active, Muse Ember’s pricing drops to 0.4 cents per million input tokens.

#5583. For Every Condo Buyer in the U.S., There Are More Than Two Sellers. That Gives Condo Buyers Strong Negotiating Power.

Condo buyers today have more negotiating power than they’ve had in at least 13 years. There were an estimated 123% more condo sellers than buyers nationwide in September, the largest gap in records dating back to 2013. The gap widened from 95.5% a year earlier.

Redfin estimates the number of buyers using proprietary data on the typical time between a buyer’s first home tour and the closing of a purchase, along with MLS data on active listings and pending sales. The estimated number of sellers is based on active listings in the MLS. The figures in this report are national estimates. See the full methodology and explore the interactive dashboard.

Redfin defines a buyer’s market as one with more than 10% more sellers than buyers, and a seller’s market as one with more than 10% more buyers than sellers. A market is considered balanced when the difference between sellers and buyers is within 10%. Other housing-market statistics, including median sale price, are based on Redfin’s analysis of MLS data.

A buyer’s market doesn’t necessarily mean condos are affordable for buyers.

The condo market has undergone a dramatic reversal since the pandemic-era homebuying boom. In September 2021, there were 25.1% fewer sellers than buyers.

Five years later, the number of buyers fell 54%, while the number of sellers rose 36%. The shift has left sellers competing for a much smaller pool of potential buyers.

The number of condo buyers fell to an estimated 88,460 in September, down 2.5 % from August and the lowest level in at least 13 years. Meanwhile, condo sellers totaled 197,248, up 0.9 % from the prior month.

Several factors are weighing more heavily on the condo market than on the single-family home market. Rising insurance premiums, HOA fees and special assessments are making condos increasingly expensive to own, particularly in Florida and Texas, where hurricane risks and other natural disasters have contributed to higher insurance costs. That’s a problem for first-time buyers, who often turn to condos as a more affordable entry point into the housing market but lack equity from a previous home sale.

While the condo market is challenging for buyers, those who can afford housing costs will have more power in negotiations.

“For renters who have saved for a down payment and are ready to build equity, these buyer-friendly conditions are an opportunity,” said Asad Khan, a senior economist at Redfin. “Buyers have more options and a better chance of finding a place they like. Although condo prices and HOA fees remain relatively high, buyers have more room to negotiate price cuts, and condos are still generally more affordable than single-family homes.”

The single-family market saw a similar trend in September, with the number of buyers dropping to a record low since 2013. Sellers outnumbered buyers by 53.7%–a wide gap, but less than half as wide as what we’re seeing in the condo market.

The huge surplus of condo sellers over buyers is contributing to the record-breaking buyer’s market in the overall housing market, which encompasses condos, townhouses and single-family homes

The national median condo sale price fell 0.8% to about $339,000 in September, the first year-over-year decline in five months.

House hunters should keep in mind that the costs of buying and owning a condo extend beyond its purchase price, and those ongoing expenses can put additional pressure on buyers’ budgets. Rising homeowners association (HOA) fees and insurance premiums can push up the total monthly cost of ownership. Buyers should also consider the possibility of special assessments to cover major repairs or improvements to a building’s common areas.

But for buyers who can afford the upfront costs of a condo and plan to stay put for several years, today’s buyer’s  market may offer an opportunity.

“Find a motivated seller and there are a lot of them,” said Cecilia Cordova, a Redfin Premier agent in Miami, who lives in a condominium herself. Researching the buildings you’d like to live in is the key to finding a financially healthy community and avoiding surprise assessment bills later, she said.

Condo buyers have more options than they did years ago. “We have enough inventory for the next three to four years,” said Cordova.

For prospective sellers? Cordova suggests considering renting their condo out for the time being. “If you really need to sell, the strategy is to list it lower than anybody else in the same building. It’s not time for you to try to experiment with a higher price,” she said.

Today’s home prices and mortgage rates have made it harder for first-time homebuyers to enter the market, reducing demand for condos, which have traditionally served as an entry point to homeownership. The weekly average mortgage rate is 7.18% as of November 5, and home prices remain near historic highs.

Sellers are increasingly dropping their asking prices to attract buyers, Redfin data shows. About 37% of condos that sold in September had a price reduction, compared with 16% during the pandemic-era housing boom five years earlier.

The typical condo that sold in September spent 63 days on the market before going under contract, up from 35 days five years earlier.

Condo buyers in Texas had more negotiating powers than anywhere else in the country in September. San Antonio had the widest seller-buyer gap among the 50 most populous U.S. metro areas, with an estimated 459% more sellers than buyers. Houston followed with 322% more sellers than buyers, then came Austin, with 258% more.

Miami also had one of the nation’s widest gaps, with an estimated 274% more condo sellers than buyers in September, ranking third.

“San Antonio condos may have an attractive purchase price, but buyers are looking at the total monthly payment. Because we have so many affordable single-family homes available, many buyers choose a house when the payments are close,” said Derrell Skillman, a Redfin Premier agent in San Antonio, TX.

Skillman added San Antonio has a large military community, and its housing market tends to follow the military’s permanent change-of-station (PCS) season.

“We usually see more military-related activity during the spring and summer when families are transferring in and out of the area. Once that period slows down, the drop in demand can be more noticeable, especially in a smaller segment like condos,” he said. “HOA costs, financing restrictions, builder incentives, softer investor demand and the slowdown after the military PCS season are all contributing to the buyer’s market for condos,” said Skillman.

Meanwhile, new construction is adding to the softness in Sun Belt markets. The Sun Belt is home to nine of the 10 metros where condo sellers outnumber buyers most.

Nassau County, NY, was the only metro area among the 50 analyzed that was a seller’s market for condos in September. There were 32% fewer sellers than buyers, with an estimated 1,545 buyers compared with 1,052 sellers.

“Condo buyers are mostly people who want maintenance-free living,” said William Ortiz, a Redfin Premier agent in Long Island, NY. “They want to have an easier lifestyle as opposed to all the maintenance and upkeep that comes with a house. Common charges are expensive, but they’re willing to pay for that convenience.”

According to Sandra Glaser, a Redfin senior agent in Long Island, condo demand is coming from three main groups: first-time buyers priced out of single-family homes, particularly those moving from the city to the suburbs; downsizers seeking less upkeep; and investors looking for rental income from properties that require minimal maintenance.

Five other metros — Chicago, Milwaukee, New Brunswick, Newark and San Francisco — had balanced condo markets, where the difference between buyers and sellers was within 10%.

San Francisco’s condo market, for example, is heating up, with the median sale price jumping 20% year over year to nearly $1.2 million in September. Khan, the Redfin senior economist, ties the area’s renewed housing demand to the AI boom, which is attracting highly paid workers and fueling homebuying.

As a senior data reporter, Dian uses data and quantitative analysis to tell stories about economy and real estate. She also builds databases and creates statistical charts that visualize data trends. Previously, Dian spent seven years as a senior data reporter at USA TODAY.

Asad Khan studies housing market trends and the forces behind them as a senior economist at Redfin. Previously, he was an economic consultant at Analysis Group where he worked on antitrust and valuation matters. Asad taught urban economics as a Research Fellow at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and earned a PhD in economics from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. His research has focused on the economics of city structure and zoning policy.

#5582. How Buyers Can Tell if a Home Price Cut Signals a True Deal

More than one in five U.S. home listings received a price cut in August, but a lower asking price does not necessarily mean the property has become a good deal. Price reductions are becoming harder for homebuyers to ignore. In August, 20.4% of U.S. listings had a price cut, matching the rate recorded a year earlier, according to the latest Realtor.com housing report.

The median asking price fell 1.3% year over year to $424,500, marking the tenth consecutive month of annual declines. Meanwhile, pending sales slipped 0.2%, ending an eight-month run of year-over-year growth.

For buyers, the growing number of reductions may look like an invitation to start bargain hunting. However, a crossed-out asking price provides little evidence of the property’s actual value.

“A price cut tells you the seller’s first number did not work. It does not tell you what the home is worth,” says Jeremy Olsher, a principal at Mizner Residential Group. “Some reductions create a legitimate opportunity. Others simply bring an unrealistic price closer to where it should have started.”

Olsher recommends three checks before treating a reduced listing as a deal.

Compare the new price with completed sales. Buyers should begin with recently sold properties that are genuinely comparable in location, size, condition and features. Active listings reveal what other sellers hope to receive, while completed sales show what buyers have accepted.

A $40,000 reduction may look substantial, but it has limited meaning if the home remains $50,000 above comparable sales.

“The percentage reduction is the part buyers notice first because it is easy to understand,” Olsher says. “The more useful question is whether the new price makes sense beside the homes that have actually sold.”

Read the entire listing history. The number and timing of reductions can reveal how the seller is responding to the market. A single adjustment after several quiet weeks may indicate growing flexibility. Several small reductions can suggest the seller is chasing the market downward without fully accepting current buyer demand.

Buyers should also check whether the home was previously listed, withdrawn and returned with a new price or description. A fresh listing date does not always mean the property is new to the market.

“Days on the market need context,” Olsher says. “I want to know whether the seller made one meaningful correction or has spent months making small changes that never addressed the real pricing problem.”

Account for condition and ownership costs. A reduced property can remain expensive once repairs, insurance, taxes, association fees and immediate maintenance are considered. Buyers should compare the home’s total financial exposure with competing properties, rather than evaluating the asking price in isolation.

A lower price may represent genuine value when the cost of resolving known issues has already been reflected. It becomes less attractive when the discount is smaller than the work or ongoing expenses the buyer will inherit.

There may also be room to offer below the revised price, particularly when comparable sales support a lower figure or the property has remained available after multiple reductions. Olsher advises buyers to base that offer on evidence rather than choosing an arbitrary percentage below asking.

“The strongest offer is not necessarily the closest to the seller’s latest number,” he says. “It is the one a buyer can explain with recent sales, property condition and realistic costs. A reduction opens the conversation. The numbers still have to hold up.”

Michael Catarevas is a senior editor for RISMedia.

#5581. Christina Haack Says She Paid Off Her College Debt by ‘Hitting It Big’ on a Las Vegas Slot Machine

Real estate investor Christina Haack doesn’t mind proving people wrong, even if that includes her own mom.

The “Flip or Flop” shared the unlikely story of her student loan payoff, after experiencing a “full circle” moment during a recent trip to Las Vegas.

In an Oct. 29 Instagram post, the HGTV personality, 43, shared a collection of photos where she’s posed in front of a slot machine while enjoying a glass of her own brand of wine, Clé Cachée.

“Really come full circle since age 21,” she explained in the caption before adding that she “paid off” her “college debt by hitting it big” on a slot machine called “top dollar.”

Haack was proud to close the loop “22 years later,” by getting to enjoy her own champagne while playing her “fav” machine. She called the experience “priceless,” and joked: “My mom always told me no one actually wins in Las Vegas. Turns out mama’s not always right.”

Her boyfriend, Chris Larocca, left a cheeky comment under the post, writing, “Maybe you have a good luck charm now…” to which she replied, “Most definitely.”

Haack has previously shared that when she was attending San Diego State, she “never thought about being on TV” and instead thought she “wanted to be a sports agent like Jerry Maguire.”

Eventually she realized she’d rather get her real estate license, and explained that she “got started in real estate at 21”—the same year she won big at a casino.

While Haack’s previous financial win may have been the luck of the draw, it’s safe to say her family is set up for success in a much more intentional way these days.

The mom-of-three recently made a splash online when she, her ex-husband Tarek El Moussa, and his new wife, Heather El Moussa, gifted daughter, Taylor El Moussa, a very expensive vehicle for her 16th birthday.

The close-knit crew of co-parents splurged on a $150,000 BMW X5, a lavish gift they said was “well deserved.”

“It’s such a beauty. I’m so happy for her,” Christina said in an Aug. 13 Instagram Reel that showcased the moment the teen was surprised with the new car, which had an enormous pink bow on it.

Heather wrote that the trio had worked together to surprise Taylor, and even joked that she was unsure if the car was more impressive, or if “the fact that three of us actually pulled this off” was a more jaw-dropping feat.

Tarek later shared more details about the purchase, explaining that the family had “good reason” to purchase the luxury vehicle during an appearance on the “Money Rehab” podcast with Nicole Lapin.

“She’s got a 4.2 GPA. She was MVP of her freshman soccer team. She’s an absolutely fantastic kid, and she didn’t just get it—she actually earned it,” he said. “If you ask me, she deserved it because she worked really, really hard.”

Noting that the car was also selected for its host of safety features, Tarek added that the vehicle was mostly his choice, as Taylor would have probably preferred a much-less-expensive Ford Bronco.

“Here’s the truth. She was flying in private jets when she was like, 1 year old,” he said. “So this kid has grown up around things. When I grew up, I didn’t have anything, right? So I’m obsessed with things because I never had things. She’s always had things.”

Staying firm in his belief that the gift was a “reward for all the work she’s done,” Tarek revealed that the family has also set her up for success financially in addition to showering her with pricey gifts.

Tarek noted that he has snapped up stocks and investment real estate for his teen daughter, and said that “if she were going to be a spoiled brat, she probably wouldn’t have got the 4.2 GPA, she probably wouldn’t have been MVP of her soccer team, and she probably wouldn’t have done the extra coaching.”

#5580. PitchBook opens its platform to startups for free and debuts Origin deal sourcing service

Private markets data provider PitchBook Data Inc. today opened its platform to startups for free at Web Summit in Lisbon.

Those that sign up have to share their financials. Some of that information will reach investors through the company’s new deal sourcing service, PitchBook Origin.

The launches come as more startups than ever are landing a first round. In the U.S., the 2021 record for first-time financings had already fallen by the end of September, PitchBook and the National Venture Capital Association found in their latest Venture Monitor report.

PitchBook credits artificial intelligence with part of that growth, since the technology has made companies easier to start. AI tools have also compressed investor diligence from weeks to days. Sourcing has not kept pace, the company argues, particularly where the signals are not public.

Free access for startups runs through a program called PitchBook for Startups. Founders who have bootstrapped or raised only from angels, grants or accelerators qualify as long as they are now seeking a first institutional round and can show at least a mockup of their product.

Once a startup has handed over its financials and details on its leadership team and product, its founders can use the PitchBook platform to research which firms are actively writing checks in their sector and stage. Investor research tops PitchBook’s own list of what founders can do with the access.

That founder data lands in a much bigger pool on the Origin side, where coverage starts at about 25 million companies and 250 million people profiles. Bootstrapped businesses and companies that have not yet raised money or announced what they are building are part of that count, and some 15 million of the companies are new to PitchBook.

Third-party data enrichment and PitchBook’s own machine learning models supply part of the coverage. PitchBook said it has not had founder-verified data at scale before.

Each company gets a score, and investors can tune relevance filters to their own criteria. Real-time alerts, saved searches and customer relationship management integrations are meant to replace the manual monitoring that deal teams do now.

Chief Solutions Officer Paul Santarelli said the missing piece for investors has been visibility into “the stage before a company raises, when the most important signals are the hardest to see.” Every company that joins the startup program and contributes verified information sharpens that picture, he said.

PitchBook “was once a startup itself, working to get in front of the right backers,” President and Chief Operating Officer Rod Diefendorf said. Founded in 2007, the Seattle company now serves more than 100,000 clients worldwide. Morningstar Inc. has owned it since 2016.

Startups can apply for the program now. Origin is available as a standalone product or as an add-on to the main PitchBook platform.

#5578. Inflation Hotter Than Economist Expectations, Raising Odds of 2027 Rate Hikes

Inflation picked up speed in October, as the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) accelerated faster than predictions from economists.

The October CPI saw the all-items index grow 0.4%, a slight decrease from last month’s 0.6% rise, but “hotter than expected,” according to Navy Federal Chief Economist Heather Long. Original forecasts were at 0.2% to 0.3% increases, as noted by Realtor.com® Senior Economist Jake Krimmel.

Inflation’s jump this month was due to increases in shelter inflation (up 0.3%), contributing to over 30% of the increase. Food inflation also advanced in October by 0.5%. Energy inflation, which decelerated in October, still saw a rise of 0.7%.

This month’s data does not include annual inflation numbers as the BLS noted it did not collect data in October 2025 due to the government being shut down at the time. As a result, it cannot calculate 12-month percent changes.

With the data available, Long said October’s increase “implies about a ~4% inflation rate for the past year.”

The index for all items less food and energy—core inflation—grew by 0.3% in October, the same rate of growth it saw in both September and August. Indexes that contributed to increase include household furnishings and operations, recreation, medical care, motor vehicle insurance and education.

Long said this month’s data “underscores why so many Americans voted the way they did in the mid-term elections,” speaking of the “blue wave” that overtook the elections last week.

“The same supply-side and geopolitical pressures are still at work, with energy playing an important role and tariff-driven goods inflation not going away,” added Krimmel. “These are the costs most salient to consumers and voters, as we saw, yet the Fed has less direct control over them.”

He noted that for the Fed outlook, a “December hike now looks almost certain, with odds jumping to 99% this morning.”

“Additional hikes in early 2027 look more in play as well, with the 10-year Treasury up 9 basis points just 25 minutes after the CPI report release,” Krimmel continued.

Looking at housing, Krimmel said that near-term there could be “upward pressure on mortgage rates again” due to rising Treasury yields and the potential of a rate hike from the Fed.

Claudia Larsen is a senior editor for RISMedia.

#5577. Sunlight, Weather and Childcare: A Year of New Data on Redfin Home Listings

In 2026, Redfin added information about sunlight, weather, childcare access and more to home listings. Here is everything you need to know about what’s new.

A home listing has always been good at telling you about a house: the square footage, the year it was built, the number of bedrooms. Historically, it has been less good at telling you what living there is actually like. Does the kitchen get morning sunlight? How hot are the summers? Is there a daycare within walking distance?

Those are the questions we set out to answer this year. Multiple new data sets arrived on Redfin in 2026, and they now sit alongside other information that was already there, including scores about a property’s walkability, transit access and climate.

Sunscore shows exactly how much sunlight a home gets

Natural light is one of the hardest things to judge from listing photos or a single showing, and it matters more than you might expect. In a recent Redfin survey, nearly 70% of people said the amount of sunlight in their home affects their satisfaction with where they live, and 11% said it is non-negotiable when searching for a home.

Sunscore is a property-level rating from 0 to 100 that shows how much sunlight a home gets. We co-created it with Shadowmap, a sunlight analysis platform, using 3D modeling that tracks how shadows fall across a home throughout the day and across the seasons. Here are the score breakdowns:

Each score accounts for the home’s 3D shape and structure, surrounding buildings, trees and terrain, the sun’s position throughout the day, and seasonal changes across the year. In other words, it catches the things you would only discover after moving in—like a neighboring building that blocks the afternoon light in winter.

And it is not only about comfort and aesthetics. A home’s sun exposure also says something about its solar potential, which can translate into real savings on energy costs over time.

Weather data helps predict precipitation and heat

Weather turns out to be one of the biggest reasons people move. In a recent Redfin survey conducted by Ipsos, 22% of Americans planning to move to another state said better weather was motivating the move—the most cited reason out of nearly 30 options, ahead of affordability, job opportunities and moving closer to family. Another 21% said concerns about climate change or natural disasters were shaping where they wanted to live.

In July, we partnered with The Weather Company, owner of The Weather Channel app and weather.com, to bring historical weather data to every for-sale listing on Redfin. As our exclusive historical weather provider, it supplies the same data hundreds of millions of people check every month.

Each listing shows ZIP code-level averages for:

Consider this information the difference between the weather on the day you tour a home and the climate you might actually live in.

Childcare data displays daycare and preschool options

For families with young children, childcare access can determine a neighborhood’s fit as much as school boundaries do. However, it’s historically been missing from the home browsing experience. Redfin is the first major real estate portal to partner with Winnie, the largest marketplace for childcare and early education in the U.S., to bring local childcare information to for-sale listings.

Nearby daycare and preschool options now appear on for-sale home listings with details that determine whether a spot is realistic for your family, such as:

Location scores capture everything from wellness access to noise

While Walk Score, Bike Score and Transit Score already existed on home listings, Redfin has expanded these location scores to capture more information about a neighborhood’s vibe using Local Logic data.

#5576. AI security startup Bay launches with $50M to vet agent actions before they run

Israeli artificial intelligence security startup Bay AI Inc. launched today with $50 million in funding to let enterprises vet each action an AI agent tries to take before it runs.

Bay provides software that tracks the agents working across a company, whether they sit on an employee’s laptop, inside a cloud workload or in a software-as-a-service application. One set of policies covers them all.

First-generation AI security tools mostly filter prompts and responses. Bay argues that misses where the damage happens, since a harmless-looking prompt can still end with an agent deleting a production database.

The founders ran into that kind of failure themselves when one of their own coding agents, working with its normal permissions, tried to expose a cloud environment to the internet to finish a test. They still have the screenshot.

Bay installs through the mobile device management or endpoint detection and response tools a customer already has, and the company says it takes under five minutes. A scanner called Wave inventories the agents, extensions and local models on each machine and leaves nothing running once it finishes.

Each time an agent proposes an action, the AI tool running it hands the request to Bay Enforcer, a static binary, through a native hook. The check happens on the machine itself with the whole session as context, and Bay said a verdict comes back in milliseconds, sometimes as a prompt asking the user to approve the step. Anything judged too risky never runs.

The policy behind those verdicts comes from Bay’s Lighthouse system, which drafts a separate one for each team from the last 30 days of agent activity, so security staff are not writing rules every time someone picks up a new tool. Teams can test a policy against the previous month first and see what it would have stopped. Bay said false positives run under 1%.

Security leaders are often handed an enterprise-wide AI rollout with a year-end deadline, co-founder and Chief Executive Yuval Zacharia said, or find that agents have already spread across the company and “it’s the Wild West.” She wants security to become “the reason AI ships faster, not the reason it stalls.”

Micron Technology Inc., Wix.com Ltd., ClickUp Inc. and Peloton Interactive Inc. are among the dozens of enterprise customers signed in the nine months since Bay was founded. Fortune 100 companies on the platform tripled their use of autonomous agents in just under 30 days, the company said.

Zacharia founded Bay with Chief Product Officer Aner Morag and Vice President of Research and Development Boris Danilovich. The three knew each other from the Israel Defense Forces’ Unit 8200, where Zacharia led a department of about 50 people before becoming the first intelligence officer there to cross into offensive cyber operations. After the military she ran security research and AI at Cyber Hunters Ltd.

Danilovich was an early employee at Preempt Security Inc. and stayed six years at CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. after it bought the startup in 2020. Most of Bay’s research team followed him over. Morag was the first employee at Noname Security.

The $50 million comes from two rounds. Battery Ventures LP led the larger $37 million Series A round, and Micron’s venture arm, Micron Ventures, also participated after the chipmaker started out as a Bay customer. Wiz Inc. Chief Executive Assaf Rappaport put in money personally. The remaining $13 million came from a previously undisclosed seed round co-led by YL Ventures Ltd. and Striker Venture Partners.

Yoav Leitersdorf, managing partner at YL Ventures, said his firm looked at a crowded field of AI endpoint security companies before picking Bay. He believes it can become “as fundamental to enterprise AI adoption as the network firewall was to the internet era.”

Engineering and product hiring will continue in Tel Aviv, where Bay is based, with the sales, marketing and customer teams growing in the U.S. and Europe. Enterprises can buy the platform now.

#5575. Police Raid $4.4 Million San Francisco Squatter Mansion—Arresting Woman and Rescuing 7 Dogs

The woman allegedly at the center of a squatting dispute in San Francisco’s luxury Sea Cliff community was arrested on Friday during a raid of the property and following a monthslong investigation into her claims on the home. Diana Peng, 42, was charged with fraud, driving without a license, narcotics possession, improper care of animals, and being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition. Police also removed seven dogs from the home and put them in the care of a local shelter.

Peng and her alleged accomplice, Brandon Aadee, are in the midst of a civil lawsuit brought by San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu. Chiu accused the pair of illegally obtaining the $4.4 million property through forged, fraudulently notarized deeds, intending to sell it.

According to Chiu’s complaint, Peng and Aadee took over the 3,000-square-foot Tudor-style home at 250 32nd Ave. in 2025 by claiming that the previous owner had transferred the deed to Aadee. Peng and Aadee transferred the property title back and forth between them eight times, and at least five of those were forged, including the initial deed from the legitimate owner, Wei Wang, which includes a forged notary signature.

Wang and her husband, Xiangdong Guo, purchased the property in 2013 for $2.41 million. But the pair moved abroad around 2019, and the property fell into disrepair and appeared to be abandoned.

It also racked up more than $340,000 in unpaid property taxes, which prevented a sale of the property.

This past October, however, the San Francisco Board of Supervisors approved a resolution to pay off the property taxes, paving the way for the home to be put up for auction later this year.

Neighbors in the wealthy enclave, where both Sharon Stone and Twitter founder Jack Dorsey have homes, said they spent much of the past year on edge, watching people come and go from the property at all hours.

"I'm probably in touch with one city official or another at least six times every day," neighbor Whitney Lynn told ABC 7. "We really have been asking for help, and it feels like people finally heard us.Most recently, in August, a neighbor called 311 to complain that the property was “being used as a group home.”

“The home was abandoned for over 5 years, and squatters moved in May 2025 using burglary tools. Over the past couple of days, a new group of about a dozen squatters moved in," the complaint read. Nearly a dozen complaints were also filed with the Department of Building Inspection, the most recent on Oct. 13. That complaint stated that unpermitted plumbing and irrigation work had been taking place in the backyard.

Neighbors told the San Francisco Chronicle that Friday’s raid lasted about four hours and that police removed several boxes and bags of documents. Police went in with guns drawn and came out with Peng, and seven dogs were removed from the property and taken to a local shelter. Police also towed Peng's Porsche.

Deb Campbell, the public information officer with San Francisco Animal Care and Control, tells Realtor.com® the two adult pit bulls and five puppies are “doing well in our care.” She otherwise couldn’t comment on the animals' condition because of the ongoing investigation.

“We appreciate SFPD’s work to pursue accountability and keep our neighborhoods safe,” Jen Kwart, the communications director for the city attorney’s office, tells Realtor.com. "As our civil case moves forward, we look forward to continuing to work closely with SFPD to ensure the courts understand that Defendants are effectively trying to steal a house and sell it to make millions in profit.”

Both Peng and Aadee have long criminal records. In 2008, she was convicted of perjury and sentenced to 90 days in jail and three years’ probation. Four years later, she pleaded guilty to identity theft and burglary and served seven months in prison. And then in 2015, she was sentenced to an additional two years in jail for forgery of a driver’s license and using another person's identification.

In 2009, Aadee was convicted of defrauding FEMA out of thousands of dollars and ordered to pay $48,000 in restitution. He also has convictions for credit card fraud and passing bad checks.

Following Friday’s raid, Peng was booked and is being held without bail at the San Francisco County Jail.

#5574. Solana Targets Durable Nonces After $270M Drift Hack as Pump.fun Backlash Grows

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Solana developers are preparing to remove durable nonces, the transaction feature exploited in April’s $270 million Drift Protocol hack. The proposed change marks a major shift in how the network handles offline approvals, with implications for exchanges and institutional custodians.

The proposal, known as SIMD-0723, would retire a mechanism that allows signed transactions to remain valid indefinitely. Attackers reportedly exploited this functionality to execute pre-approved transactions more than a week after obtaining signatures from Drift’s security council.

Solana wants to kill the feature behind April's $270M+ Drift hack.SIMD-0723, filed Nov 5 by Anza, would retire "durable nonces": signed transactions that never expire. Normal Solana transactions go stale in ~30 seconds. Earliest switch-off: May 5, 2027. pic.twitter.com/VYYttCsvJk

The move comes as Solana faces another challenge closer to its retail ecosystem. Pump.fun is facing growing community criticism over platform fees, influencer promotions, and allegations of hidden-wallet trading. Together, the developments put renewed attention on security, transparency and trust across Solana’s ecosystem.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

Normal Solana transactions use recent blockhashes that expire after 30 seconds. Durable nonces replace those temporary references with stored values, allowing transactions to remain executable until the nonce advances.

The feature was designed for legitimate operational needs. Exchanges, custodians, and multisig organizations often require offline signing procedures that take longer than Solana’s normal transaction window.

However, attackers turned that convenience into an attack vector against Drift on April 1, 2026. They reportedly secured administrative approvals through air-gapped signing systems before allowing the transactions to sit for more than a week.

Once submitted, the approvals helped attackers take control of the protocol and drain at least $270 million. Drift subsequently attributed the attack to a North Korean-linked group.

Anza contributor Gabe Rodriguez filed SIMD-0723 on November 5. The proposal would require transactions to use recent blockhashes after activation. May 5, 2027, represents the earliest proposed mainnet activation date. The change still requires technical approval and migration planning.

Solana is also exploring replacement programs that could support offline signing without relying on durable nonces. These alternatives would introduce different authorization and transaction-failure considerations for custodians.

The proposal forces institutional users to reconsider how they authorize transactions across Solana. Meanwhile, questions about trust are becoming harder to ignore elsewhere in the ecosystem.

Pump.fun has attracted fresh criticism following several developments involving its business model and influencer ecosystem.

On November 6, blockchain tracker Lookonchain reported that Pump.fun transferred 76,111 SOL, worth approximately $6.85 million, to Kraken. The movement reignited criticism over platform fees and whether its incentives adequately serve ordinary traders.

Pump fun(@Pumpfun) is dumping $SOL again!They just deposited 76,111 $SOL ($6.85M) into #Kraken.In total, https://t.co/TcwYRTArT2 has sold 5,553,833 $SOL($882.4M) at an average price of $158.88.https://t.co/kyztoJLCjt pic.twitter.com/QvzqaR8fGI

Bubblemaps also accused prominent influencers of using undisclosed wallets to purchase tokens before publicly recommending them. Its investigations estimated $125,000 in combined trading profits and promotional rewards involving influencer Ethan.

Separate allegations involving paid streamer collaborations surfaced on November 7. The revelations have intensified questions about transparency within Pump.fun’s promotional ecosystem.

These controversies involve different problems from Drift’s exploit, but they expose a similar challenge: maintaining confidence among participants.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

That challenge also creates an interesting opportunity for Bitcoin-focused projects exploring alternative execution environments.

Bitcoin Hyper is developing a Bitcoin Layer 2 using Solana Virtual Machine technology. Its architecture aims to combine SVM’s high-speed execution with Bitcoin-based settlement, bringing smart contracts, decentralized exchanges, and staking functionality to BTC.

Bitcoin Hyper is not simply another Solana application. Its design uses SVM execution while anchoring Layer 2 state to Bitcoin through periodic commitments and zero-knowledge proofs.

This combination gives it a different proposition from Solana-native applications. Developers can work with an execution environment associated with Solana’s performance, while the project targets Bitcoin’s established settlement infrastructure.

Bitcoin Hyper has also reached several development milestones. Its testnet is live, with a public explorer allowing users to inspect transactions and network activity.

The project’s presale has raised approximately $33.2 million, with HYPER priced at a low $0.0136 per coin. Its November 26 presale deadline leaves 17 days from today for prospective participants to enter before the planned launch window.

The upcoming transition toward mainnet, wallet infrastructure, and exchange listings puts the project in an important stage of development. Its combination of Bitcoin settlement and SVM execution gives it a distinct position in the expanding Bitcoin Layer 2 sector.

#5573. The 5 Biggest Mistakes Veteran and Military Homebuyers Make

Having a place to call your own—whether it's your starter home or your forever home—is an essential part of the American dream. And the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs offers plenty of great programs to help those who have served in the military become first-time homebuyers.

However, the process to get a home loan as a veteran isn’t foolproof.

"Being eligible for a VA loan and ultimately able to secure one are different things," explains Chris Birk, vice president of mortgage insight and education at Veterans United Home Loans. "Prospective buyers will still need to meet credit, income, and other guidelines set by both the VA and by the lenders that make these loans."

You can set yourself up for success before you even start your home search and avoid making missteps that have held other prospective homebuyers back.

We asked VA-savvy real estate agents to tell us which missteps they see the most—and how you can avoid them when you apply for and get a VA loan.

If you’re getting a VA loan, make sure you work with a real estate agent who understands the VA home loan process.

“The VA won’t underwrite [just] any house," says Katie Fraser, a Realtor® with Keller Williams Tacoma. "It is a huge, huge, huge deal to use an agent who understands the VA home loan system, the VA appraisal process, and what that all really looks like.”

When you’re buying through the Veterans Affairs Department, you’ll need to find a home that meets VA home loan property requirements. A VA loan program appraiser will have specific criteria. An agent experienced with home loans for veterans will also know about VA loan limits, the debt-to-income ratio lenders will expect you to have to qualify for a home loan, and other essential information.

So, save yourself the heartache of making an offer on a house that may not get approved, or for which you may not qualify for a VA loan, and work with a VA-experienced real estate agent from the start. Ask another veteran for a referral, or get help from Veterans United Realty to find the right real estate agent.

Veterans have access to arguably the most powerful home mortgage option on the market, yet still far too many veterans don’t know about VA loans.

When you first talk with your lender, be sure to discuss your service history so you can be informed about all of the potential advantages for veterans.

One of the biggest benefits you’ll get with a VA loan is the ability to buy with a 0% down payment (yes, we're totally serious). Not having to make a down payment can make it possible for veterans  to buy a first home, often years sooner than if they had to save up for a down payment first.

VA loans also come with low-interest-rate mortgages, don't require private mortgage insurance, and have more forgiving credit eligibility requirements.

"Veterans should ask their lender if they offer any incentives for veterans," adds Alissa Gerke, broker and owner of Select Realty Group in Columbia, MO. "I’ve seen lenders waive appraisal fees, offer a waiver of origination fee if the veteran has a certain credit score, or other lender credits."

Pretty much everything will get easier as soon as your lender knows you're a veteran or service member, so speak up!

While you'll have a ton of financial advantages with your VA loan, you will have some borrower costs to deal with.

“Probably the biggest mistake I see is active-duty members coming into the homebuying process and not knowing there are other closing costs and fees necessary for buying a home,” Fraser says.

When you’re buying a home, even if you have little or no down payment, you’ll likely have to plunk down a bit of cash for things like a home appraisal and inspection. It might not cost much in the large scheme of things, but it'll help speed things along if you come prepared knowing what you'll have to shell out for.

Maybe you think there's no sense in buying if there's a chance you might be relocated in the next few years. But that doesn't mean you shouldn't buy. In fact, that home could end up being a smart investment.

By searching in high-demand areas or choosing a popular home style and size (say, 1,500 to 2,000 square feet), you’ll give yourself a better chance at resale if you need to move later. Or, you can hang on to it and rent it out.

My clients and I "often go out and look for their first rental home, not just a home for their family," Fraser says. "With so many in transition, they’re able to purchase a home and it becomes an investment property for them when they go on to their next duty station or they move.”

Don’t like the idea of becoming a landlord? A VA loan is assumable (meaning you can transfer the loan and the property to another person), or you can just sell the home and regain your full VA loan entitlement.

Don’t forget: You can use your VA home loan benefits again and again, so you can own a rental property and a new home. You can even refinance a VA loan if you are an active-duty service member. You may want to refinance if you have a non-VA loan, want to increase your loan amount and tap into your home equity, or want to get a better interest rate with a new VA loan.

Once homebuyers find a home and their offer is accepted, they can be excited about moving in and making it theirs. Maybe you have an eye on a new big-screen TV, and you're looking into financing a new living room set you love. But don’t do that until you're really a homeowner, even if your lender has approved your mortgage loan.

It's easier to get a VA loan than a conventional, non-VA loan, but you still must meet lender requirements.

“Opening a line of credit or making a big purchase after mortgage approval is a common mistake,” Gerke says. “This can oftentimes change the veteran's credit score and make them ineligible for the loan.”

Wait until after closing to make any other financial moves, just to be on the safe side and to keep your loan on track.

Angela Colley writes about real estate and all things renting and moving for Realtor.com. Her work has appeared in outlets including TheStreet, MSN, and Yahoo.

#5571. Teleport makes Beams generally available to bring AI agents into production

Infrastructure identity company Teleport today made Teleport Beams, its runtime for artificial intelligence agents that work on production infrastructure, generally available.

Beams goes after what Teleport sees as the main reason agents have stayed out of production so far. Most enterprises have not plugged agents into those systems at all, according to Ev Kontsevoy, Teleport’s co-founder and chief executive. He blamed gaps such as delegated identity and an audit trail that follows an agent from intent to action.

Sandboxes, the tool many teams reach for now, mostly isolate the agent in a virtual machine and handle its credentials. “When the cost of an error is high, traditional sandboxes don’t cut it,” Kontsevoy said ahead of the announcement.

Teleport calls each individual runtime a Beam, and every agent gets its own. A Beam carries a delegated identity inherited from the user or agent that launched it, while the agent inside starts with no standing privileges. Work begins with a proposed execution plan. That plan can be revised by a person or by a large language model acting as judge before a separate Beam runs it with only the approved roles. Reviewers then see new requests only for steps outside the plan.

Passwords never enter the agent’s environment. Everything the agent sends to a model is traced, and Teleport says that record lets Beams pick out a hijacked goal or agents coordinating in ways nobody planned. Each session also gets scored against the MITRE ATT&CK framework for a written risk summary. Seven of the detection rules come prebuilt, privilege escalation among them. Anything else a customer wants caught can be described in natural language and added to the set.

Each Beam is an ephemeral micro-VM on a virtualized network. Nothing gets in or out without passing Teleport’s controls, and the audit log keeps a copy of every protocol exchange. Snapshots taken by a feature named Phases carry the files and memory of an expiring Beam into the next one, so longer jobs do not have to start over.

Teams can also fork a Beam to try several approaches in parallel. When something goes badly wrong, a kill switch ends the agent’s activity and cuts all of its connections to production at once.

Teleport makes no promise about what a model will decide. A hijacked or mistaken agent inside a Beam can reach only what it was granted until its authority lapses at the end of the task, and every action it takes stays on the record.

Beams runs on top of the Teleport Infrastructure Identity Platform, which the company says is in production at more than 700 enterprises, Nasdaq Inc., DoorDash Inc. and Elastic N.V. among them. Cisco Systems Inc. became Teleport’s largest strategic investor in August.

Teleport first showed Beams in March, two months after publishing the Teleport Agentic Identity Framework that the runtime now puts into practice. Following a public beta, the product is available at beams.run.

#5570. October Marks the First Month in 3 Years With a Decline in U.S. Home-Sale Prices

For three years, U.S. home-sale prices rose from a year earlier every single month, even as mortgage rates climbed and would-be buyers pulled back. That streak has ended.

The median home-sale price declined 0.4% year over year to $388,634 in October. That’s  the first decline since May 2023 and a sharp slowdown from the 2.5% gain just two months earlier. With Americans’ wages growing about 4% year over year, even a slight dip in prices can improve affordability. Sale prices have risen nearly every single month for the last 13 years; the only exception was a handful of months in 2023.

With the total number of homes for sale at its highest level since early 2020 and demand cooling, homebuyers’ negotiating power keeps increasing–and that’s finally showing up in sale prices.

Home-sale prices fell nationwide, but they rose in more than half of the 50 most populous U.S. metro areas. San Francisco led the nation by a wide margin, with the median sale price rising 16.8% year over year. That’s the biggest increase since 2018. Next comes New Brunswick, NJ, with a 7.7% gain. Two other NYC-area metros also had price increases ranking in the top six; the median sale price rose 4.4% in both New York City and Nassau County.

In San Francisco, AI wealth is fueling competition for scarce inventory; active listings were down 7% from a year earlier. In the New York City area, years of limited homebuilding have left buyers competing for relatively few homes in a region with a strong job market.

Home-sale prices fell most in Austin, TX, where they declined 6.5% year over year. It’s followed by Seattle (-5.1%) and Nashville, TN (-4.9%). Austin and Nashville are among the biggest buyer’s markets in the U.S., and Seattle’s shaky tech job market is curbing demand.

National sale prices are losing steam because fewer Americans can afford to buy a home. U.S. pending home sales fell 3.6% from a month earlier in October on a seasonally adjusted basis to their lowest level since 2013, with the exception of April 2020.

This is a real-time indicator of the state of the housing market; fewer homes went under contract in October largely because mortgage rates averaged 7.33%, a three-year high and up from 6.86% the month before.

All figures in this report are seasonally adjusted, with the exception of median sale price data and mortgage rate data. See a more detailed methodology here and view an interactive dashboard here.

“It’s a buyer’s market, but not many people can afford to buy,” said Chen Zhao, Redfin’s head of economics. “That could start to shift a bit, now that sale prices are closer to reflecting the shape of the market. House hunters in most of the country should know that the price they see on a listing may very well be a starting point; they should try offering below the asking price, and negotiating for closing costs, repairs and maybe even mortgage-rate buydowns. If you can’t get the price or monthly payment you want on one house, move on to the next one–with a big pool of inventory sitting on the market, buyers can afford to be picky.”

Pending home sales declined in all of the most populous U.S. metros. That’s the second month in a row that has happened; before September, the last time was three years earlier.

The biggest declines were in Seattle and San Diego, both places where pending sales fell more than 20% year over year. Those West Coast metros are some of the priciest in the U.S., so 7%-plus mortgages hit house hunters’ monthly payments there hard. In Seattle, an uncertain local job market is also curbing demand.

Closed home sales fell to their lowest level in nearly 3 years. They declined 2.1% month over month in October to their lowest level since December 2023; before that, the last time sales dropped that low was 2014. Many of the deals that closed last month went under contract in August and September, when rates were already climbing and economic uncertainty was deterring a lot of house hunters.

With homebuying demand falling, supply is building. The total number of homes for sale rose 0.9% from September to its highest level since early 2020; that’s the biggest monthly gain since May 2025.

More supply gives buyers more homes to choose from and more leverage:

“Buyers are nervous about rates, the economy, and everything they’re seeing in the news– so they need the house and the price to line up perfectly before they’ll make an offer,” said Callie Kimmel, a Redfin Premier agent in Philadelphia. “I’m advising sellers to price just below current market value from day one–and not comps from six months ago, but homes that are listed right now. Otherwise, the home is likely to end up sitting on the market for a bit and selling for less than they hoped. There are a few exceptions: Move-in ready homes in the most desirable neighborhoods are still competitive; in those cases, sellers have the upper hand.”

While total housing supply is growing, fewer sellers are adding new inventory to the pool. New listings of homes for sale fell 1% month over month to the lowest level in more than two years. Would-be sellers are pulling back as homebuying demand slows and sale prices lose steam.

The figures below are based on a list of the 50 most populous U.S. metropolitan areas. Some metros may be removed from time to time to ensure data accuracy. Refer to our metrics definition page for explanations of metrics used in this report. All changes below represent year-over-year changes.

#5569. Billy Joel Is Returning to the Stage—Months After Selling His Long Island Estate and Revealing Brain Disorder

Billy Joel is returning to performing—months after he offloaded his Long Island estate and nearly one year after revealing a brain disorder diagnosis.

The hitmaker, 77, revealed in a Nov. 9 social media post that he would be making his on-stage comeback.

“Florida Atlantic University will welcome singer, songwriter, and composer Billy Joel for Billy Joel: An Evening of Questions & Answers…And a Little Music,” he penned on Instagram, alongside a snap of himself singing.

The post revealed that he would be performing on Dec. 14, adding that tickets would be exclusively available to currently enrolled students at FAU.

This will mark Joel's first official performance since he announced on May 23 that he would be calling off his tour in order to focus on treatment for normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH)—which occurs when there's a buildup of fluid in the brain, causing difficulty walking and balancing, confusion, and forgetfulness, per the Cleveland Clinic.

According to a statement released by the singer's spokesperson on Instagram, his condition has been "exacerbated by recent concert performances, leading to problems with hearing, vision, and balance," forcing him to bow out of his planned tour dates.

“Under his doctor’s instructions, Billy is undergoing specific physical therapy and has been advised to refrain from performing during this recovery period. Billy is thankful for the excellent care he is receiving and is fully committed to prioritizing his health," the announcement continued.

The statement added that the "Piano Man" singer was thankful for his fans' "support" and that he "looks forward" to performing when his health is in a better place.

"I'm sincerely sorry to disappoint our audience, and thank you for your understanding," Joel added in a quote.

At the end of the statement, fans were reassured that they won't need to take any action to receive their refunds, adding that their payments will be automatically refunded to the original form of payment.

The concert dates that were affected by the news include shows in New York City; New Orleans; Toronto; Santa Clara, CA; Salt Lake City; Washington, D.C., and Liverpool.

Months after he announced his diagnosis, his daughter, Alexa, gave fans a long-awaited update on her dad's performance schedule, telling the Hollywood Reporter that he is a "trooper."

She noted that her father was looking forward to returning to Carnegie Hall on March 19, where his daughter will be belting out his hits at a tribute event.

Alexa explained, “I said, ‘Dad, you better be there! This is Carnegie Hall. Everyone’s paying tribute to you, and it’s an amazing group of artists.' He was like, ‘Let me mark that down.’ He’s very organized with his little calendar. He was so excited when he first played Carnegie Hall in the ‘70s, so it’s exciting for him to come back decades later and see amazing artists and his daughter pay tribute to him. It’s a full-circle moment."

The 40-year-old singer-songwriter also noted that her father's health is much better.

"He’s doing physical therapy regularly, and he’s doing great," she revealed. "He’s lost weight as he’s on his diet. I’m so proud of him. He’s such a trooper, so resilient and committed to being healthy and proactive. He’s a fighter. He’s always been a fighter and talks in his documentary about how life’s like a fight.”

She added, "He played it down. He knows I have anxiety and am a neurotic worrier, so he was, like, ‘Everything’s fine. It was just a little trip.’ When I saw the footage, I was crying. But then I went with him to the doctors, and we’re on top of everything. I just tell him to stay healthy.”

“Once a performer, always a performer! But health comes first. I said, ‘If you’re going to perform again, please stay seated at the piano. No throwing the microphone stand around!’" she revealed.

Alexa's update on her father's health came mere weeks after he finally offloaded his Long Island estate.

Joel had been trying to sell a large portion of his Long Island estate since March 2025, when it was listed for $39.9 million, having initially put the entirety of the property, which is made up of three parcels, on the market for the even higher price of $49 million.

However, after months with no concrete offers, the asking price of the property's main residence was slashed, first to $29.9 million, then to $25 million.

In 2025, he sold the seven-bedroom, nine-bathroom gatehouse for $7 million. On March 6, 2026, Billy sold the main property—dubbed "Middlesea"—for $23.2 million, as well as a pair of adjoining lots that brought the total to $35.75 million.

He purchased his Long Island sanctuary in 2002 for $22.5 million before picking up two adjoining plots.

The main residence, which comes with 14.6 acres, was formerly on the market for $25 million, while the two adjacent plots were listed for $3.5 million each.

When deciding to separate the areas, Emmett Laffey, CEO of Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices Laffey International Realty, said, "The new price reflects the splitting of the two buildable waterfront lots, so the gross price remains the same."

“When [Billy Joel] bought this 20 years ago, he bought the main house. And then as he lived there, he bought the adjacent two lots, which are buildable lots, and he purchased a gatehouse. Now we’re selling it like he bought it—in pieces. The smartest way to sell this incredible land and property is the way he purchased it," Laffey previously told the Post.

Laffey noted that many super "fans" have already attempted to snap up the property and have put in several offers.

“You do have some extreme fans. It is very special. It’s a very famous home to everyone on the North Shore of Long Island," he said.

The main house sprawls over 20,000 square feet and comes with five bedrooms, six full baths, two half-baths, a playroom, a spa and hair salon, a bowling alley, and a wine cellar.

There's also an indoor pool, which Billy had covered up so he could use the space as a music room, because of its excellent acoustics.

The estate also features a three-bedroom beach house, a three-bedroom guest apartment, and a four-bedroom gatehouse, which has since been sold.

Other luxe amenities include a floating dock and boat ramp, two outdoor pools, and a helipad.

Billy previously insisted that he would still call Long Island home, but would be spending more time in Florida.

Although Billy and Alexa tend to focus on music, they have previously exchanged real estate, with him having sold his Manhattan property, a two-bedroom condo, for $4.5 million to Alexa.

Despite passing the dwelling to his own family member, the singer didn't hold back with the price, earning an impressive $1.2 million profit on the $3.3 million he paid for the Elizabeth Street dwelling in 2010, when he purchased it from his then-wife, Katie Lee.

Property records now reveal that the two-bedroom, two-bathroom dwelling has been transferred to Alexa following a $4.5 million transaction, as first reported by Crain's.

The home, which sits at 211 Elizabeth St., spans 1,600 square feet. Pre-staged photos revealed dark herringbone floors, black crown moldings, and a dark-toned chef's kitchen, according to Curbed.

Transferring the property into his daughter's name was a formality for the most part, as it has been reported that Alexa has been living in the dwelling since 2010.
